bubbleNote.blurb: Alabama sits on the 13 line, one spot outside the field -- the closest team to the cut and the first in line if anyone above stumbles.
LSU holds the 14 seed, two spots from the field, and gets an immediate chance to move: No. 23 Clemson comes to Baton Rouge next.
USC is the No. 15 team in the bubble picture, three spots out, and needs results rather than reputation to close that gap.
BYU occupies the last bubble spot at No. 16, four spots from the field -- the Cougars have the most ground to make up of anyone still in the conversation.

games.blurb: No. 13 LSU opens with a heavyweight, laying 10.5 on No. 23 Clemson in a Week 1 matchup with a 50.5 total that suggests points will be at a premium. The loser starts the year with a résumé dent it can't fix in September.
The Apple Cup returns with No. 19 Washington favored by 21.5 at home. Rivalry or not, the Huskies are being asked to look the part of a ranked team from the opening snap.
Louisville heads to Oxford as a 6.5-point underdog against No. 10 Ole Miss, with a 55.5 total pointing to a shootout. A tighter spread than most top-10 openers, and the Rebels know it.
No. 5 Notre Dame is a 20.5-point favorite over Wisconsin with the total sitting at just 47.5. The Irish are expected to win comfortably; the question is whether they do it with style points.
The Border War kicks off the weekend with Colorado State favored by four at home. Four points in a rivalry game means nobody should be surprised by anything.
No. 16 Michigan opens as a 26.5-point favorite over in-state visitor Western Michigan. A tune-up on paper, and the Wolverines will take it that way.

predictions.blurb: Texas checks in at No. 4 with FPI slotting the Longhorns even higher at No. 2 -- the metrics see a legitimate SEC and national title contender.
Texas Tech sits No. 12 in the poll and No. 10 in FPI, the rare Big 12 team the numbers and the voters largely agree on.
Michigan lands at No. 16 with FPI a tick more bullish at No. 15 -- essentially a consensus read on the Wolverines as a solid but unproven Big Ten piece.
BYU is No. 15 in the poll but only 20th in FPI, making the Cougars one of the more skeptically viewed ranked teams in the Big 12.
LSU opens at No. 13 while FPI has the Tigers up at No. 9 -- the analytics think there's room to climb, starting Week 1.

fieldStorylines.blurb: The Big Ten's automatic bid is a two-team argument: No. 1 Ohio State and No. 2 Oregon are separated by a single spot, so the league's playoff path likely runs through whichever of them blinks first.
Georgia holds the SEC's auto-bid position at No. 3 with Texas breathing down its neck at No. 4. One slip from the Bulldogs and the Longhorns are ready to take it.
Texas Tech leads the Big 12 race at No. 12 with BYU three spots back at No. 15 -- a real gap, but not a comfortable one over a full season.
